name: Mihkel Aamer

education.notes: Five-year integrated masters; self-taught programming alongside an engineering-design curriculum rather than pure CS.

keyDecisions: Left Estonia for the UK at 18 — chose a higher-prestige engineering programme over staying local.
Picked engineering design rather than pure CS — kept systems-thinking lens but had to self-teach code.
lessons: A general engineering degree plus self-taught coding can be a stronger founder-prep mix than narrow CS — broader systems intuition with enough code to be dangerous.
Geographic mobility at 18 is a cheap option to take — relocation costs are low when you own nothing.

keyDecisions: Sampled deep-tech (HP, Motorola) and finance (UBS) before committing to a domain — refused to pick early.
lessons: Internships across very different industries are cheap optionality — you learn which culture you want to scale inside before you have to commit.
A finance internship is not 'selling out' if you treat it as an option you can let expire.
careerSteps.notes: Approximate years inferred from undergraduate timeline; exact internship dates not public.

keyDecisions: Joined Wise pre-scale (~2013) rather than chasing a higher graduate salary — bet on equity and operating reps.
Stayed ~6 years through growth-stage to pre-IPO — built deep institutional knowledge of European fintech regulation.
Worked through enough seniority levels to become Head of Engineering before leaving — earned operator credibility, not just tenure.
lessons: Operating at a category-leading scale-up in your target domain is a faster founder-school than a generic MBA — the network, the regulatory experience, and the equity all compound.
European-fintech 'mafias' (Wise, Skype, Stripe) form when many strong operators leave one company at similar life stages — being inside one when it scales is the cheapest way to acquire that network.
Optimise for the company's growth curve, not your title — a 6-year run at Wise produced more option value than a 6-year ladder at a bank.
careerSteps.notes: Reported by FintechFutures, Crunchbase, and Lightyear press materials as a senior engineering lead and eventually Head of Engineering. Exact title-progression dates not public.

keyDecisions: Co-founded with fellow ex-Wise alum Martin Sokk — pre-existing trust shortened partner vetting from months to zero.
Built for European retail investors specifically (multi-jurisdiction, EU regulatory) rather than cloning Robinhood — leaned on the exact regulatory expertise the team already had.
Raised first cheques from the Estonian / Wise-network angels (Hinrikus, Tallinn, Villig) before chasing brand-name VCs — used the mafia network as proof, not as a fallback.
Founded at 31 after operator depth — explicitly rejected the 'found in your 20s' script.
lessons: Personal frustration as market signal: Aamer's own friends asked him which European broker to use and there was no clean answer — that gap became the company.
If your target market is regulated and multi-jurisdiction, a co-founder pair where both have operator credibility in that space is worth more than a deck.
Founder age is downstream of category — for regulated fintech, the 30+ founder with 5+ years of regulated-product experience beats the 22-year-old dropout.
careerSteps.notes: Lightyear markets commission-free but earns on FX and money-market spread; expanded to 25 European countries and 5,000+ instruments. ~$23M round in 2025 with Richard Branson, Taavet Hinrikus, Jaan Tallinn, and Ahti Heinla / Villig family on the cap table.

outcomes.currentStatus: Co-founder & CTO of Lightyear, a pan-European commission-free retail investing platform. No exit; equity value paper-only and dependent on next-round outcomes.

lessons.lesson: Personal frustration as market signal — friends asking which broker to use, and Aamer not having a clean answer, exposed the European retail-investing gap.
Spend 5+ years inside the regulated category you want to disrupt before founding in it.
Co-founder selection from the same operator alumni network compresses trust-building time from months to zero.
Found at 31, not 21, when the category demands regulatory depth.

notes: Post-2020 European fintech founder; Wise-mafia alumnus. Highly replicable template for a European technical operator: top engineering degree (with self-taught code on the side) → ~6 years at a category-defining scale-up in your target vertical → spin out at 30+ with a co-founder from the same alumni network and seed cheques from that network. Caveat: Lightyear has not yet had a liquidity event, so the financial outcome is unproven. Most years (Wise role progression, internship dates) inferred — confidence is medium overall.
